key_insight: MLExpert shows that a generalist agent can learn autonomous long-horizon machine learning engineering by turning multi-step experiment feedback into training signal.
engineering_relevance: This work points to a practical path for AI systems that can independently run, revise, and optimize ML experiments with less human intervention.
method: Built Kaggle-MLE Factory to generate executable MLE tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation.
Used hierarchical agentic SFT to transfer general tool-use and coding skills into machine learning engineering workflows.
Introduced Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL), which groups decisions between experiment results into windows and assigns shared outcome-based rewards.
evidence_signal: On MLE-Bench Lite, the model's average medal rate rose from 37.9% to 72.7%, and it also generalized to NatureBench Lite, scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization.
watch_item: Because training depends on costly long-horizon trajectories and windowed outcome rewards, performance may be sensitive to task design, feedback quality, and asynchronous policy correction.
paper_title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
